limits: The byte-identical assertion covers the general LUKS image during the ephemeral workload, not the entire USB.
The quota test forces tmpfs ENOSPC; it does not test physical-memory OOM or power loss.
The TUI uses a synthetic provider; no real Abliteration request.
The host runs under Mac HVF and the nested guest under TCG; production x86/KVM isolation is not tested.
Temporary new API credentials, live USB integration and real Tor ephemeral use remain open.
The ephemeral network workload uses an external synthetic SOCKS/provider; actual Tor bootstrap, tool circuit isolation and real provider behavior remain separate gates.
